title: I've been making a hybrid Visual Novel heavily utilizing the AI tools for the last year and I'd like to show you a trailer
author: tmk_lmsd
selftext:
Roche.Limit is a mystery thriller about a girl who wanted to start a new life, but pretty much fucked everything up, went into huge debt - and now the world is in great danger. Then one night she meets a mysterious fox-eared girl in her apartment who swears she has always lived there.

The game takes place in New Warsaw, Poland in the distant future, the main protagonist is Japanese with Finnish ancestry. I don't want to spoil the main plot here but I believe it catches off-guard.

It'll have 3 languages: Polish, English and Japanese.

The story, characters and world are mine. AI helps me draft and polish, fix grammar errors and bullshit my bad English produces. but every decision and the final text go through me.

I’ve already spent a couple hundred dollars on tools. If you’re curious, the workflow:

1. Graphics: mostly GPT Image, plus local models in InvokeAI (Krea, Anima) and manual touch-ups. I create 3D scenes in Blender and use them as a template for further work, this way I can have the same location made from different shots, consistently.
2. Music and sounds: Suno, then my own mastering and editing in Audacity. I also record sound effects with my microphone or use Pixabay.
3. Claude and ChatGPT work in tandem as two "team members" with their own names - one writes code, the other reviews it, and they catch each other’s bugs and plot holes. I approve what goes in.
4. Systems so far: VN exploration, a mobile phone, a computer, a map, top-down RPG Maker sections and a few minigames with rewards. Also some simple stealth mechanics
5. The story will have 5 acts and 3 playthroughs, each a different experience. Right now I’m wrapping up Act 1.

For VN standards my solutions are unorthodox and not really visual novely but I trust my own vision.

Main inspirations: Steins;Gate, Undertale, Ib, The Longest Journey, Syberia, old point-and-click adventures and PSX games. I also wove in things that inspired me as a child or left a lasting memory. I hid a lot of references to popculture I personally liked and enjoyed

One of the main design ideas is empty spaces - I believe silence can deliver as much as actual content so there may be moments that are slice of lify or idyllic but they're met later with brutal change of pace that the reader may wish he'd like to go back when things were silly and normal

I also avoid wider marketing for now because the game is just not ready yet. Unfortunately, there's no way of following the game anywhere if that peaked your interest but I'll consider putting my development online one day. Maybe itch or steam we'll see

  
My dream is to show the other people that AI is just a means to achieve a heart-warming story I always wanted to tell since I was a kiddo

Hope you find it interesting.

comments.author: LucianAshford13
comments.body: using blender scenes as a base for consistent AI generated backgrounds is an interesting approach, has that helped reduce the amount of time u spend fixing inconsistencies between shots?

replies.author: tmk_lmsd
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/meo0a6ho2myh1.png

  
Oh, definitely. I often have to retouch the details and such but it still feels like it's the same location, the same scene. One of my main problems I wanted to solve "I have a front shot of a character but I really want a side shot now, how do I do that without everything breaking apart?" and that solved it mostly
